instructions.name: claim_hole_share
docs: An early feeder collects their share of a collapsed star.

instructions.name: claim_prize
docs: The Star Killer collects the jackpot.

accounts.name: winner
docs: Checked against `star.killer` in the handler (the star account is
deserialized after this one).

instructions.name: close_push
docs: Return a finished push account's rent to the player. Optional cleanup.

accounts.name: player_wallet
docs: only there. Not `SystemAccount` for the same reason as the refund
destination above - see `ResolvePush::player_wallet`.

instructions.name: close_round
docs: Seal the star's open round and fix its ORAO seed. Permissionless, moves
no lamports. Allowed once the round's window has elapsed or it is already
full enough that waiting would only add latency - and once the batch's
own rake covers what ORAO currently charges for a draw. A round that has
not earned its draw yet stays open and keeps collecting members.

accounts.name: cranker
docs: Anyone. Touches no lamports at all.

accounts.name: slot_hashes
docs: `vrf::recent_slot_hash`. Sampled here for seed material only.

accounts.name: vrf_network_state
docs: to price the draw this seal commits the house to buying. No CPI.

instructions.name: create_first_star
docs: Birth star #1. Permissionless, once. Uses `Config.genesis_seed`.

instructions.name: create_next_star
docs: Birth the next star after the current one has died. Permissionless.

accounts.name: payer
docs: Permissionless. Pays rent for the new star account.

instructions.name: expire_round
docs: Void a round that has been stalled for `ROUND_EXPIRY_SLOTS`, making all
of its members refundable. Permissionless. Refuses if the draw has
already landed, so it can never be used to duck an unfavourable roll.

accounts.name: vrf_request
docs: the draw has *not* landed. Ignored while the round never got as far as
being requested, in which case the address is still default.

instructions.name: feed
docs: Nursery hole ticket. One signature, instant settle, no VRF.
Clips to leftover room; fails if the nursery is already full.

instructions.name: fund_protocol
docs: Donate lamports into the protocol balance, which is what randomness is
bought out of. Needed once at bootstrap, because the rake cannot accrue
until a push settles and a push cannot settle until a draw is paid for.

instructions.name: initialize
docs: Create `Config` and the vault. Once, by whoever deploys. The signer is
only a payer - no authority is stored, because none is ever used.
* `genesis_seed` - visual seed for star #1. Later stars derive theirs
from their predecessor's death randomness.
* `treasury` - where `withdraw_protocol_fees` sends protocol revenue.

accounts.name: payer
docs: Pays rent for `Config` and tops the vault up to rent exemption.

accounts.name: vault
docs: The one SOL vault. System-owned with zero data, so the program can
move lamports out with a signed `system_program::transfer` and nothing
else can touch it.

instructions.name: request_push
docs: Last-hit: escrow the stake and join the star's open round. The player's
only signature, and the only lamports it moves are the stake - the draw
this push will roll against is bought later, once, for the whole round,
out of the protocol's own balance.
* `star_id` - must be the current live star; recorded permanently on
the push so it can never roll forward to a later star.
* `client_seed` - 32 random bytes from the client. Two jobs: it scopes
this push's address within the player's own wallet, and it is folded
into the round's entropy accumulator. It is *not* a VRF seed, so
reusing one after `close_push` is harmless.

accounts.name: round
docs: The star's open round. Created by whoever gets there first and shared by
everyone who arrives before it is sealed.
Pinned to `star.current_round` by seed, so a player cannot pick which
round to join - in particular they cannot re-join a round whose seed is
already fixed, because `close_round` bumps this counter as it seals.

accounts.name: pending_push
docs: Scoped to the player so two people pushing in the same slot can never
collide on this address, and `init` stops one player double-spending a
`client_seed` that is still in flight. Reuse after `close_push` is
harmless now: `client_seed` only feeds round entropy and this PDA, and
`push_id` comes from the star's counter, which never repeats.

instructions.name: request_round_vrf
docs: Buy the one draw that serves a sealed round. Permissionless; the signer
fronts ORAO and is reimbursed from `protocol_accrued`, capped at what the
rake actually holds so the game cannot stall for lack of funds.

accounts.name: vrf_request
docs: sealed seed derives, and must not exist yet.

instructions.name: resolve_push
docs: Settle or refund a push. Permissionless; the player never signs again.
While the star is alive, `push_id` must equal `star.settle_cursor`.
A refund does not require fulfilled randomness.

accounts.name: resolver
docs: Anyone. Pays the transaction fee and nothing else - every account this
instruction touches already exists.

accounts.name: star
docs: Pinned by seed to the star the push was aimed at, so a draw can never be
resolved against a different star.

accounts.name: round
docs: Pinned by seed to the round this push joined, so it can only ever settle
against the draw it committed to before that draw's seed existed.

accounts.name: player_wallet
docs: else. Deliberately *not* `SystemAccount`: that would additionally
require the wallet to still be owned by the system program, and a
player who assigns their account to some other program - which the
system program lets them do with their own signature, irreversibly -
would have their stake locked in the vault forever with no instruction
able to release it. A system transfer only constrains its source, so
paying out to a non-system account is perfectly legal.

accounts.name: vrf_request
docs: and seed are all re-checked before use, and `round.status` must be
`Requested`, so only a draw this program bought can ever be read.

accounts.name: star_feed
docs: Both of these were created and paid for by `request_push`, so the
resolver never funds an account here.

instructions.name: withdraw_protocol_fees
docs: Move accrued protocol revenue to the treasury frozen at initialize.
Anyone can crank it. Cannot touch escrowed pushes or unclaimed prizes.

accounts.name: crank
docs: Anyone. Pays the transaction fee.

types.name: Config
docs: Singleton game state: where the money is owed, and which star is live.
It holds no tunable parameters. Odds, bounds and splits are compiled into
[`game_config`](crate::game_config) and cannot be changed by any
instruction.

fields.name: treasury
docs: Destination for `withdraw_protocol_fees`. Frozen at initialize.

fields.name: current_star_id
docs: 0 until the first star is created.

fields.name: genesis_seed
docs: Visual seed for star #1. Later stars hash the previous star's seed.

fields.name: pending_liability
docs: Stake escrowed by pushes that have not been settled or refunded yet.
Not part of any jackpot until the push resolves against a live star.

fields.name: prize_liability
docs: Prize money owed to (current + past) star killers, claimed or not.

fields.name: protocol_accrued
docs: Protocol revenue, and the float randomness is bought out of. The only
balance `withdraw_protocol_fees` can touch, and the only balance
`request_round_vrf` can reimburse a crank from.

fields.name: next_star_reserve
docs: Recycled prize waiting to seed the next star. Not withdrawable.

types.name: FeedShare
docs: One wallet's hole ticket on one star.

types.name: LifecycleConfig
docs: The stage table, frozen onto each star at birth.

types.name: PendingPush
docs: One push. Created when the player signs, permanently bound to the star
they meant to push and to the round whose draw decides its fate.
Field order up to `amount` is fixed by the Android hand-decoder, same as
[`Star`]; see the layout test at the bottom of this file.

fields.name: star_id
docs: The star this push was aimed at. Never rolls forward to a later star.

fields.name: amount
docs: Escrowed stake, in lamports.

fields.name: round_id
docs: The draw this push shares. Recorded at request time, before that draw's
seed is decidable, which is the entire anti-grinding argument. Filed
after `amount` rather than next to `push_id` so the two offsets above
stayed where the hand-decoder already looks.

fields.name: roll_ppb
docs: Populated on a settled (non-cancelled) resolve.

fields.name: chance_ppb
docs: Nova chance quoted at request time, against committed mass. For
display only: the authoritative threshold is computed at settle from
settled mass and written to `threshold_ppb`. The two differ when the
queue moved in between, and the difference never changes the push's
expected value.

fields.name: stardust_mult_bps
docs: Stage dust multiplier frozen at request (queue-aware stage).

fields.name: client_seed
docs: This member's contribution to its round's entropy, and the second half
of this account's own address. Appended rather than filed next to
`round_id` so the hand-decoded offsets above did not move.
Kept on chain rather than only in the request event so that a round's
seed is verifiable from account state alone: fold every member's
`client_seed` in `push_id` order, mix in the slot hash `round.seed_slot`
names, and the result has to equal `round.seed`.

types.name: Player
docs: Lifetime stats per wallet. STARDUST is internal points only - there is
deliberately no SPL token in this MVP.

types.name: ProtocolFunded
docs: Lamports were donated into `protocol_accrued`, which is the float
`request_round_vrf` reimburses cranks from.

fields.name: amount
docs: Refunded in full, in the same transaction.

fields.name: round_voided
docs: True when the refund is because this push's round was voided rather than
because the star had already finished. The star is still alive in that
case and the player can push again immediately.

fields.name: round_id
docs: The draw this push will share. Its seed does not exist yet.

fields.name: client_seed
docs: This member's entropy contribution, published so the round's seed can be
replayed from events alone.

fields.name: round_members
docs: How many pushes were sharing the round at this point, including this
one. The oracle cost is divided by its final value.

fields.name: chance_ppb
docs: Nova chance quoted against committed mass at request time, for display
while the push is in flight. `PushResolved.threshold_ppb` is the one
that was actually rolled against.

types.name: PushResolved
docs: A push settled against a live star.
Field order up to `threshold_ppb` is pinned by the Android log parser; see
the layout test in this module.

fields.name: stake_refund
docs: Stake handed back in this same transaction because the room left at
settle was below what the queue quoted at request time. `amount` is
already net of it.

fields.name: survived
docs: false means this push destroyed the star.

fields.name: threshold_ppb
docs: `amount / star_mass` in ppb: the push's share of the mass it created.

fields.name: star_mass
docs: Star mass after this push landed.

types.name: Round
docs: One VRF draw, shared by every push queued while it was open.
This is what makes the oracle affordable: ORAO charges per request, not per
player, so a round of `n` pushes costs `1/n` of a request each. It is also
what makes the randomness cheap to *verify* - there is one draw and one
published seed per batch, and each member's roll is a labelled hash of it.
## Why the seed is safe
The seed must not be computable by anyone until the round is sealed,
otherwise somebody buys the draw early, reads it, and only pushes when the
roll would be lethal. Two ingredients, each covering the other's gap:
* **`entropy`**, folded from every member's `client_seed` as they join. A
player can steer their own contribution, so this alone is not enough.
* **a slot hash sampled at close**, which nobody can predict - not the
members, and not whoever submits the close, since the draw that seed
produces does not exist yet and cannot be shopped for.
Members are therefore committed before the seed is decidable, and the seed
is fixed before the draw is bought. Nothing to grind at either end.

fields.name: entropy
docs: Running hash of every member's `client_seed`. Half of the seed input.

fields.name: seed
docs: The ORAO seed, fixed at close. Zero while the round is open, which is
the honest representation: it is genuinely not decided yet.

fields.name: randomness
docs: ORAO randomness account for `seed`. Default while open.

fields.name: seed_slot
docs: Slot whose hash went into `seed`, so the derivation can be replayed
off-chain from public data alone.

fields.name: member_count
docs: How many pushes share this draw. The divisor on the oracle cost.

fields.name: stake
docs: Total escrowed stake of those members. Not accounting - this is what
decides whether the round has earned its draw yet. See
[`Round::covers_draw`].

fields.name: first_push_id
docs: `push_id` of the first member, so a client can enumerate the batch.

fields.name: opened_slot
docs: Slot the first member arrived, i.e. when the window started.

types.name: RoundClosed
docs: A round was sealed and its ORAO seed fixed. Emitted by `close_round`.
Everything needed to verify the seed independently is here: the sampled slot
is named, and the members' contributions are in their `PushRequested`
events. No draw exists at this point.

fields.name: seed_slot
docs: The slot whose hash went into `seed`.

fields.name: randomness
docs: ORAO randomness account to watch for fulfillment.

fields.name: stake
docs: Total stake behind the draw, and the rake it will yield. Published so the
economic gate is auditable after the fact: `rake >= draw_cost` held here,
or the star was full and took its last draw on the house.

fields.name: forced
docs: True when the round was sealed under the full-star exemption, i.e. it
could not grow any further so waiting for a bigger batch was impossible.

types.name: RoundExpired
docs: A round stalled and was voided. Emitted by `expire_round`. Every member is
now refundable through `resolve_push`, in any order.

fields.name: never_sealed
docs: True when the round never even got sealed, i.e. nobody cranked it.

types.name: RoundRequested
docs: The one draw for a whole round was bought. Emitted by `request_round_vrf`,
the only place the protocol pays ORAO.

fields.name: payer
docs: Whoever fronted ORAO and was reimbursed.

fields.name: cost
docs: What the request cost after the rent ORAO returns on fulfill. Measured
across the CPI, not assumed.

fields.name: reimbursed
docs: What the rake could actually cover. Below `cost` only when the protocol
balance is short, in which case `payer` absorbed the difference.

fields.name: cost_per_member
docs: `cost / member_count`: what randomness worked out at per push.

types.name: RoundStatus
docs: Where a [`Round`] is in its life. The order matters: a round only ever
moves forwards, and only `Requested` permits a push to settle.

types.name: StageConfig
docs: One lifecycle stage: the mass at which it begins and how much STARDUST it
mints.
Deliberately carries no odds. Stages are cosmetic and economic flavour now;
lethality is [`nova_ppb`], which is structural.

fields.name: min_mass
docs: Inclusive lower bound, in lamports of star mass, for this stage.

fields.name: stardust_mult_bps
docs: STARDUST multiplier in bps (10000 = 1×). Early stages mint more.

types.name: Star
docs: Permanent record for one star. Never mutated once dead, apart from the
one-shot `prize_claimed` and `next_star_created` latches.

fields.name: seed
docs: Deterministic procedural visual seed. Drives the whole Three.js look.

fields.name: stage
docs: Index into `self.lifecycle.stages`.

fields.name: successful_pushes
docs: Pushes that settled against this star while it was alive and landed
mass. Not the settle cursor - an expired round advances the cursor
without landing anything. See [`Star::settle_cursor`].

fields.name: pending_pushes
docs: Requested but not yet resolved.

fields.name: pending_lamports
docs: Escrowed lamports of those pending pushes. Reserves room against the
hole cap so the queue cannot commit past it.

fields.name: cancelled_pushes
docs: Arrived after death and were refunded.

fields.name: push_counter
docs: Monotonic per-star push numbering. Assigned at request; settle order
follows it while the star is alive.

fields.name: total_mass
docs: Total lamports that successfully landed. Drives the lifecycle stage.

fields.name: prize_pool
docs: Prize share accumulated so far (`prize_bps` of settled mass), plus any
endowment in full. This is what a kill pays out, and the odds are the
push's share of `total_mass`, so a star with no endowment returns
exactly `prize_bps` and an endowed one returns better.

fields.name: lifecycle
docs: Stage table, copied from the compiled lifecycle at birth, so an upgrade
cannot move a running star's STARDUST taper. The odds are not in here:
they are `amount / mass_after`, which no table can change.

fields.name: death_randomness
docs: Full 64-byte VRF output of the lethal push, kept so anyone can verify
the death independently.

fields.name: death_roll_ppb
docs: The roll that was taken, and what it had to beat.

fields.name: current_round
docs: The round `request_push` currently stamps onto new pushes. Bumped by
`close_round`, and by `expire_round` when it voids a round that never
got that far, so a fresh push always lands somewhere still open.

fields.name: settle_cursor
docs: The next `push_id` allowed to resolve while the star is alive.
Every push is processed exactly once and ids are dense from zero, so
this is just "how many have been dealt with" - which makes it an exact
ordering guard. It counts refunds from an expired round as well as
settles, because otherwise a voided batch would wedge every push behind
it forever.

fields.name: echo
docs: SOL recycled into `next_star_reserve` when `early_volume == 0`. Zero if feeders exist.

fields.name: stranded
docs: True when the star collapsed short of the hole cap because it had run out
of ways to ever be pushed again, rather than by surviving to 21 SOL. Only
reachable after a voided round; see `resolve_push::stranded`.

fields.name: seed
docs: Procedural visual seed.

fields.name: derived_from_star_id
docs: Star id this seed was derived from; 0 for the genesis star.

fields.name: endowment
docs: Inherited jackpot/mass from the previous star's next-star reserve.

fields.name: killer
docs: The Star Killer.

fields.name: killer_round_id
docs: The round whose draw killed the star. `randomness` below is that draw,
and the roll is `sha256("soldust:roll" || randomness || killer_push_id)`.

fields.name: randomness
docs: Full VRF output, for independent verification.

types.name: StarFeed
docs: Early-feed tally for one star. Created on the first push.

fields.name: early_volume
docs: Settled lamports pushed while mass was still below 1 SOL.
